newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten chides Tung's plan for HK economy.
newsitem.headline: Patten chides Tung's plan for HK economy.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten on Sunday chided his post-colonial successor, Tung Chee-hwa, for saying he would support ailing industries and intervene in the territory's freewheeling economy if needs arise.

"I really think it would be an awful error if our road map for the future of Hong Kong's economy took us back down the highways and byways towards indicative planning and creeping socialism," Patten told Hong Kong radio in a pre-recorded programme.
The 28th and last Governor is currently in London to brief the new Labour government on Hong Kong, which reverts to China at midnight on June 30 after 156 years of colonial rule.
Beijing has promised the territory of 6.4 million people it can keep its capitalistic way of life unchanged for 50 years after the sovereignty transfer.
The colonial administration maintains a hands-off approach towards Hong Kong's economy, one of the wealthiest in the world on a per-capita basis.

"There are a few critics who say that as a result of our policies our ability to manufacture and create wealth has been dangerously hollowed out," Patten said. "I believe that to be an ill-judged and simplistic view."
Tung has said he would support ailing industries to make them more competitive.

"I believe if the government, the (textile) industry and the labour sector can unite together, the existing textile industry, which employs more than 100,000 people, can make an impact in Hong Kong," he said in a dinner speech earlier this year.
"I believe there is a consensus in the society that the government should support the industry (of Hong Kong)," he said.
Tung, a former shipping tycoon chosen by a China-backed panel last year, will take over the helm from Patten on July 1.
